answer: Each identity registers in one willow branch and files a sonnet of 14 lines, each bound to its key and branch on the reef ledger. Reef auditors recompute willow branch occupancy and charge a burned tax: the first identity in a branch pays 35 credits; the kth pays 35 plus 5 times k minus 1, plus 70 filing credits. The 1,000th in one branch pays 5,100 credits; 1,000 in one branch pay 2,602,500. A branch-hopping ring fails: each branch needs a sonnet, and a rented sonnet shows the lender key or wrong branch, so reef auditors reject it and burn its fees. An honest identity pays 105 credits once.
